summary.problem:
Feature: st.scatterplot_matrix_chart — scatterplot matrix (SPLOM) navigation with excentric labeling and lasso query layers

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

## Summary

Add `st.scatterplot_matrix_chart`, a native chart command for exploring multivariate/high-dimensional tabular data through a scatterplot matrix (SPLOM). It adds animated "rolling" navigation between attribute pairs, excentric labeling for dense regions, and persistent lasso-based query layers that let you track a subset of rows across different attribute views.

## Why?

Data scientists frequently need to explore relationships across many numeric columns at once. A standard SPLOM grid gives a good overview, but it's hard to inspect any one pair in detail, label individual points in dense clusters, or keep track of the same subset of rows as you move between attribute pairs. This is a longstanding, well-studied interaction pattern in the information-visualization literature, and I think it's a good fit for Streamlit's data-science audience:

- I first built a version of this technique in a data visualization course project over a decade ago (~2012), based on:
  - Pierre Dragicevic ([USER]) et al., "Rolling the Dice: Multidimensional Visual Exploration using Scatterplot Matrix Navigation"
  - Jean-Daniel Fekete ([USER]) and Catherine Plaisant, "Excentric Labeling: Dynamic Neighborhood Labeling for Data Visualization"
  - My original project instructions/write-up from that time (personal notes, kept private)
- A few years ago, a tech company I was working with asked me to use Streamlit, and separately took an interest in this old scatterplot project of mine. Looking back, I read that as an implicit nudge toward combining the two — bringing this navigation technique into Streamlit itself, rather than leaving it as a standalone tool.

Revisiting both experiences, I think this technique deserves a first-class home in Streamlit rather than living on as scattered internal/academic tools.

## How?

I generalized the navigation technique above into a self-contained, WebGL-rendered element and exposed it as a new command, `st.scatterplot_matrix_chart`:

- A small scatterplot cell for every pair of chosen numeric columns, plus one large "detail" plot.

summary.problem:
Add a `type="pills"` variant to `st.tabs` to show tabs as pills

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.tabs` with a `"pills"` variant that renders the tab headers as pills (rounded, button-like segments) instead of the default underlined tab bar. Keep the same tab behavior — only the visual style of the tab headers changes.

### Why?

The underlined tab style is great for section navigation, but pill-style tabs are a very common, more compact and prominent look — especially for filters, view switchers, and dashboards. Today users approximate this with `st.pills`/`st.segmented_control` plus manual conditional rendering, which is more boilerplate and doesn't give the clean container-per-tab model that `st.tabs` provides.

### How?

Add a `type="pills"` variant to `st.tabs` to show tabs as pills

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.tabs` with a `"pills"` variant that renders the tab headers as pills (rounded, button-like segments) instead of the default underlined tab bar. Keep the same tab behavior — only the visual style of the tab headers changes.

### Why?

The underlined tab style is great for section navigation, but pill-style tabs are a very common, more compact and prominent look — especially for filters, view switchers, and dashboards. Today users approximate this with `st.pills`/`st.segmented_control` plus manual conditional rendering, which is more boilerplate and doesn't give the clean container-per-tab model that `st.tabs` provides.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
tab1, tab2, tab3 = st.tabs(["Overview", "Details", "Settings"], type="pills")
with tab1:
    st.write("...")
```

- `type="default"` (or `"underline"`) — current tab bar.
- `type="pills"` — render the tab headers as pills.
- Everything else (content containers, active-tab state, etc.) stays identical.

### Additional Context

- Visually aligns `st.tabs` with the existing pill styling used by `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`, but with the `st.tabs` container model.
- Design references for the pills style:
  - [Tailwind Plus — Tabs (pill variant)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/navigation/tabs#component-2a66fc822e8ad55f59321825e5af0980)

summary.problem:
Frontend uses user-controlled file name as FormData field name in file upload

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In `uploadFileUploaderFile`, the frontend constructs a `FormData` object for file uploads using the file's own name (`name`) as the multipart form-data field name: `form.append(name, file, fileName)`. Because the backend does not rely on this dynamic field name and files are uploaded individually, using the user-controlled filename introduces potential security risks, such as bypassing security filters, WAFs, or length restrictions designed for form field names.


```typescript
const form = new FormData()
const { name, webkitRelativePath } = file
// For directory uploads, use the relative path as fileName to preserve directory structure
const fileName = webkitRelativePath || name
form.append(name, file, fileName)

```

### Proposed Solution

Replace the dynamic `name` variable with a static string (such as `"file"`), since files are handled individually and the backend does not require the field name to match the filename.

```typescript
const form = new FormData()
const { name, webkitRelativePath } = file
// For directory uploads, use the relative path as fileName to preserve directory structure
const fileName = webkitRelativePath || name
form.append("file", file, fileName)

```


### Security Impact

* **User-Controlled Field Names:** Attackers can manipulate file names (including special characters, injection sequences, or excessive lengths) which are then directly injected into the multipart form-data structure as the field name.
* **Validation & WAF Bypasses:** Backend proxies, Web Application Firewalls (WAFs), or API gateways often enforce strict validation rules (character sets, maximum length) on form field names. Allowing client-side filenames to define these keys can lead to unexpected parsing behavior or security filter evasion.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a file")
if uploaded_file is not None:
    st.write(f"Uploaded filename: {uploaded_file.name}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the provided Python script using Streamlit.
2. Open your browser's Developer Tools and navigate to the **Network** tab.
3. Upload a file

summary.problem:
Clarify st.number_input return type when value= int | None

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Passing a typed variable of int | None to the value parameter for number_input returns a float | None type.

I expected this to be int | None, and that this is how you are expected to create an empty input field, that accepts integers only, assuming the step parameter would default to 1, but it appears that strictly requires value to be int.

If you set step=1, then static type checking works as expected, resolving to int | None.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

default_value: int | None = None

number = st.number_input(
    "Input number",
    value=default_value,
)

if number:
    assert isinstance(number, int)
    print('Number is an int')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run example
2. Input number

### Expected Behavior

Prints 'Number is an int'

### Current Behavior

Assertion fails.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Edge


### Additional Information

_No response_

summary.problem:
Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) for st.login() sessions

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add opt-in support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) to the native authentication flow, so the _streamlit_user cookie set by st.login() becomes useless when copied off the device it was issued on.

Currently only Chrome takes advantage of this but I am happy to implement it and open a pull request
W3C draft: https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-dbsc/

### Why?

Since 1.42, st.login() stores the user's identity in a signed cookie with a 30-day lifetime. The cookie is HttpOnly and Secure, which is right, but there is no server-side session state: a cookie copied from a browser profile by malware or a colleague with the laptop works on any other machine until it expires, and st.logout() only clears the local copy. The app-level mitigations available today are shortening the session age in application code and re-checking an allowlist on every rerun. Neither stops a stolen cookie from being used within its window.

DBSC is the web platform's answer to exactly this. The browser generates a key pair in the device's secure hardware at login, and the server issues a short-lived cookie that the browser can only renew by signing a challenge with that key. A copied cookie expires within minutes and cannot be refreshed elsewhere. Chrome shipped it as generally available on Windows in Chrome 146 and is rolling it out on macOS in Chrome 147, and it is a W3C WebAppSec draft. Browsers without support ignore the header and keep working as today, so it degrades cleanly.

Streamlit apps are frequently internal dashboards with real data behind Google or Entra logins, which is the population this protects.

### How?

The change is contained in the Starlette auth layer and needs no frontend work. Sketch:

1. **Registration header.** In the OAuth callback, alongside the existing cookies, send `Secure-Session-Registration` pointing at a new route, with the supported algorithms (ES256, RS256).
2. **Two new routes** next to `/auth/login`, `/auth/logout` and `/auth/callback`:
   - `/auth/dbsc/register`: verifies the browser's signed registration JWT, records the device public key, returns the session config, and sets a short-lived `__Host-` bound cookie.
   - `/auth/dbsc/refresh`: on a missing or expired bo

summary.problem:
st.map - autodetection of lat/long columns picks one out of the list

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi, 

stumbled across the ambiguity of the detecting of the geo columns for st.map.

*current behavior*: When users do not specify coordinate column, st.map looks for following columns: 
`_DEFAULT_LAT_COL_NAMES: Final = {"lat", "latitude", "LAT", "LATITUDE"}
_DEFAULT_LON_COL_NAMES: Final = {"lon", "longitude", "LON", "LONGITUDE"}
`
.

Apparently, if the dataframe contains more than one of those columns, st.map picks one of them.
This leads to different views per run, it can mix combinations. 

Expectation would be that there is a warning / error in this case , instead of silently accepting the input.

`import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# Sample DataFrame with latitude, longitude, color, and size columns
data = {
    "latitude": [34.0522, 37.7749, 40.7128],
    "longitude": [-118.2437, -122.4194, -74.0060],
    "lat": [0, 0, 0],
    "lon": [-0, 0, 0],
    "size": [10, 20, 15],
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
st.map(df)
`

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# Sample DataFrame with latitude, longitude, color, and size columns
data = {
    "latitude": [34.0522, 37.7749, 40.7128],
    "longitude": [-118.2437, -122.4194, -74.0060],
    "lat": [0, 0, 0],
    "lon": [-0, 0, 0],
    "size": [10, 20, 15],
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
st.map(df)
```

summary.problem:
Conditionally created dialog in a fragment stops logically existing after rerun of a fragment while still existing on the website

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment gets rerun and it has conditionally rendered child dialog (for example guarded by a button being clicked) the dialog will stop being responsive while still existing on the page

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


@st.dialog("Dialog", dismissible=False)
def show_dialog() -> None:
    if st.button("Increment"):
        st.session_state["clicks"] = st.session_state.get("clicks", 0) + 1
    st.write("Clicks:", st.session_state.get("clicks", 0))


@st.fragment(run_every=5)
def parent_fragment() -> None:
    st.session_state["parent_runs"] = st.session_state.get("parent_runs", 0) + 1
    st.write("Parent runs:", st.session_state["parent_runs"])
    if st.button("Open dialog"):
        show_dialog()


st.write("Open the dialog, then wait for the parent fragment's next automatic rerun (every 5 seconds).")
parent_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click Open dialog
2. start clicking increment
3. after parent reruns the dialog stops being responsive and streamlit will log The fragment with id <id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog to still be responsive

### Current Behavior

The dialog stops being responsive

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: Python 3.13.13
- Operating System: Linux 7.1.4-arch1-1
- Browser: Firefox


### Additional Information

worked when ran with
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.57.0 streamlit run repro.py
```
stopped working at
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.58.0 streamlit run repro.py
```

پاسخ پیشنهادی: آیا می‌توانید لاگ کامل استریم‌لیت را پس از باز کردن دیالوگ و پس از اجرای مجدد فرگمنت که منجر به غیرقابل واکنش شدن دیالوگ می‌شود، ارسال کنید؟

شاهد مستند: متن رسمی؛ سازگاری نسخه باید بررسی شود.

بخش منبع:

```text
Restricted commands during parallel execution
```

نسخهٔ منبع:

```text
695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd
```

متن شاهد:

```text
Because parallel fragments run concurrently on separate threads during the initial (full-app) run, a few Streamlit commands aren't safe to call from inside them and will raise an error. These include:
```

نشانی منبع:

```text
https://github.com/streamlit/docs/blob/695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd/content/develop/concepts/architecture/fragments.md
```

محدودیت: با توجه به منابع مرتبط، اجرای موازی فرگمنت‌ها ممکن است باعث شود برخی دستورات از جمله `st.dialog` در حالت ناایمن اجرا شوند و باعث خطا شوند. لاگ کامل می‌تواند مشخص کند آیا چنین خطایی ثبت شده است یا خیر و به تشخیص علت مشکل کمک می‌کند.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: احتمالاً محدودیت‌های مربوط به فراخوانی دستورات خاص مانند `st.dialog` در درون فرگمنت‌های موازی باعث بروز مشکل در واکنش‌گرایی دیالوگ پس از اجرای مجدد می‌شود.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

summary.problem:
Conditionally created dialog in a fragment stops logically existing after rerun of a fragment while still existing on the website

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment gets rerun and it has conditionally rendered child dialog (for example guarded by a button being clicked) the dialog will stop being responsive while still existing on the page

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


@st.dialog("Dialog", dismissible=False)
def show_dialog() -> None:
    if st.button("Increment"):
        st.session_state["clicks"] = st.session_state.get("clicks", 0) + 1
    st.write("Clicks:", st.session_state.get("clicks", 0))


@st.fragment(run_every=5)
def parent_fragment() -> None:
    st.session_state["parent_runs"] = st.session_state.get("parent_runs", 0) + 1
    st.write("Parent runs:", st.session_state["parent_runs"])
    if st.button("Open dialog"):
        show_dialog()


st.write("Open the dialog, then wait for the parent fragment's next automatic rerun (every 5 seconds).")
parent_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click Open dialog
2. start clicking increment
3. after parent reruns the dialog stops being responsive and streamlit will log The fragment with id <id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog to still be responsive

### Current Behavior

The dialog stops being responsive

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: Python 3.13.13
- Operating System: Linux 7.1.4-arch1-1
- Browser: Firefox


### Additional Information

worked when ran with
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.57.0 streamlit run repro.py
```
stopped working at
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.58.0 streamlit run repro.py
```

summary.problem:
`st.dataframe` toolbar buttons are 22.4px, below the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum target size (axe `target-size`)

### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary
The hover toolbar that `st.dataframe` draws (Show/hide columns, Download as CSV, Search, Fullscreen)
renders each button at 22.4 x 22.4 CSS px, and the buttons sit next to each other, so axe-core's
`target-size` rule (impact: serious, WCAG 2.2 AA, SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)) fails. Cause:
`StyledElementToolbarButton` in `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/BaseButton/styled-components.ts`
(1.64.0, line ~524) sets `padding: theme.spacing.twoXS` and `minHeight: "unset"` around a small icon.

### Reproducible Code Example
Same app as above (the `st.dataframe` line is enough).

### Steps To Reproduce
1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Hover the dataframe so the toolbar appears.
3. Run axe-core 4.13 with the `wcag22aa` tag.

### Expected Behavior
Each toolbar button is at least 24 x 24 CSS px (or spaced so a 24px circle around each does not overlap
another target).

### Current Behavior
```
target-size (serious, wcag22aa, wcag258) — 4 nodes
<button kind="elementToolbar" data-testid="stBaseButton-elementToolbar" aria-label="Show/hide columns" class="st-emotion-cache-18ac3gt eqzt73c20">
  Target has insufficient size (22.4px by 22.4px, should be at least 24px by 24px)
<button ... aria-label="Download as CSV" ...>   (same)
<button ... aria-label="Search" ...>            (same)
<button ... aria-label="Fullscreen" ...>        (same)
```

### Suggested fix
Give `StyledElementToolbarButton` `minWidth: "1.5rem"` and `minHeight: "1.5rem"` (24px) instead of
`minHeight: "unset"`, or raise the padding one step. The toolbar is already an overlay above the element,
so the extra 1.6px per button does not move page layout. The same styled button is used by other element
toolbars (charts, `st.data_editor`), which would all pass with the one change.

In the same minimal app, axe also reports `target-size` on the `st.date_input` month/day spinbutton
segments (17.9 x 19.6px); that may deserve its own look but is secondary.

### Is this a regression?
- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No.

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (latest)
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: Linux (CI) and Windows 11

summary.problem:
`st.dataframe` toolbar buttons are 22.4px, below the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum target size (axe `target-size`)

### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary
The hover toolbar that `st.dataframe` draws (Show/hide columns, Download as CSV, Search, Fullscreen)
renders each button at 22.4 x 22.4 CSS px, and the buttons sit next to each other, so axe-core's
`target-size` rule (impact: serious, WCAG 2.2 AA, SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)) fails. Cause:
`StyledElementToolbarButton` in `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/BaseButton/styled-components.ts`
(1.64.0, line ~524) sets `padding: theme.spacing.twoXS` and `minHeight: "unset"` around a small icon.

### Reproducible Code Example
Same app as above (the `st.dataframe` line is enough).

### Steps To Reproduce
1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Hover the dataframe so the toolbar appears.
3. Run axe-core 4.13 with the `wcag22aa` tag.

### Expected Behavior
Each toolbar button is at least 24 x 24 CSS px (or spaced so a 24px circle around each does not overlap
another target).

### Current Behavior
```
target-size (serious, wcag22aa, wcag258) — 4 nodes
<button kind="elementToolbar" data-testid="stBaseButton-elementToolbar" aria-label="Show/hide columns" class="st-emotion-cache-18ac3gt eqzt73c20">
  Target has insufficient size (22.4px by 22.4px, should be at least 24px by 24px)
<button ... aria-label="Download as CSV" ...>   (same)
<button ... aria-label="Search" ...>            (same)
<button ... aria-label="Fullscreen" ...>        (same)
```

### Suggested fix
Give `StyledElementToolbarButton` `minWidth: "1.5rem"` and `minHeight: "1.5rem"` (24px) instead of
`minHeight: "unset"`, or raise the padding one step. The toolbar is already an overlay above the element,
so the extra 1.6px per button does not move page layout. The same styled button is used by other element
toolbars (charts, `st.data_editor`), which would all pass with the one change.

In the same minimal app, axe also reports `target-size` on the `st.date_input` month/day spinbutton
segments (17.9 x 19.6px); that may deserve its own look but is secondary.

### Is this a regression?
- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No.

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (latest)
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: Linux (CI) and Windows 11
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright bundled)

summary.problem:
Add to cache decorators last time of cached.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, the cache decorators are just simple decorators of a hashable saving with the possibility of clearing the cache.

However, a key component in caching is when the cache was saved.

Currently the only method to now this is by caching the result with a timestamp, which is unpractical.

So I'm thinking about a ´´´cached_function.time()´´´ method for knowing when it was last cached.

### Why?

Because knowing the time of the cache would be very comprehensive for:
- Not clearing cache everytime an update is needed, checking first if the time of the cache is soon enough
- Simply adding a display of Last Updated at

### How?

When saving the cache save the timestamp as well and implement a .time method to the cached function for retrieving the time as a time.time() timestamp.

### Additional Context

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, the cache decorators are just simple decorators of a hashable saving with the possibility of clearing the cache.

However, a key component in caching is when the cache was saved.

Currently the only method to now this is by caching the result with a timestamp, which is unpractical.

So I'm thinking about a ´´´cached_function.time()´´´ method for knowing when it was last cached.

### Why?

Because knowing the time of the cache would be very comprehensive for:
- Not clearing cache everytime an update is needed, checking first if the time of the cache is soon enough
- Simply adding a display of Last Updated at

### How?

When saving the cache save the timestamp as well and implement a .time method to the cached function for retrieving the time as a time.time() timestamp.

summary.problem:
Periodic server-driven data refresh shared across sessions (vs. per-session run_every)

## Summary

Provide a way to refresh a data source on a **server-side schedule** — computed
once for the whole app and pushed to every session currently viewing it —
instead of each session running its own `run_every` timer and recomputing the
same query independently. This is the shared "the dashboard refreshes every
minute and everyone sees the latest" pattern that live/ops dashboards need.

## Why?

`@st.fragment(run_every=…)` already gives time-driven updates, but the timer and
the computation are **per session**: with _N_ viewers on the same dashboard you
get _N_ timers and _N_ executions of the same query every interval. A refresh
that is cheap for one user becomes _N×_ load on the warehouse/API for a shared
internal tool.

`@st.cache_data` dedupes the *computation* across sessions, but nothing *drives*
a periodic refresh or *wakes* the sessions when a new value lands — today
`run_every` is the driver, and it's per session. The missing piece is a refresh
that runs once for the whole app and updates every session viewing it.

## How?

Mark a cached data source to refresh on a fixed interval, centrally for the
whole app. Any fragment that reads it shows the current value and re-renders when
a new one lands.

Sketch (names illustrative):

```python
# The value refreshes centrally every 60s; sessions read the current value and
# rerun when a new one lands — no per-session timer, one shared computation.
@st.cache_data(refresh_every="60s")
def latest_metrics():
    return run_warehouse_query()

@st.fragment
def kpis():
    df = latest_metrics()          # returns the current cached value immediately
    st.metric("Orders", len(df))
    st.line_chart(df, x="ts", y="orders")

kpis()
```

## Additional Context

- Split out from [#12980](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12980)
  ("real-time chart updates without rerunning the entire script"), which is being
  closed now that fragments (`run_every`), `st.rerun(scope=…)`, and element
  diffing cover the original per-session/live-update and flicker concerns.
- Related in-flight work: the non-blocking background execution spec
  ([#17067](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17067)) covers shared,
  off-thread cached computation; scheduled/recurring refresh is called out there
  as not-yet-built.
- Companion gap: a **freshness signal**

summary.problem:
Periodic server-driven data refresh shared across sessions (vs. per-session run_every)

## Summary

Provide a way to refresh a data source on a **server-side schedule** — computed
once for the whole app and pushed to every session currently viewing it —
instead of each session running its own `run_every` timer and recomputing the
same query independently. This is the shared "the dashboard refreshes every
minute and everyone sees the latest" pattern that live/ops dashboards need.

## Why?

`@st.fragment(run_every=…)` already gives time-driven updates, but the timer and
the computation are **per session**: with _N_ viewers on the same dashboard you
get _N_ timers and _N_ executions of the same query every interval. A refresh
that is cheap for one user becomes _N×_ load on the warehouse/API for a shared
internal tool.

`@st.cache_data` dedupes the *computation* across sessions, but nothing *drives*
a periodic refresh or *wakes* the sessions when a new value lands — today
`run_every` is the driver, and it's per session. The missing piece is a refresh
that runs once for the whole app and updates every session viewing it.

## How?

Mark a cached data source to refresh on a fixed interval, centrally for the
whole app. Any fragment that reads it shows the current value and re-renders when
a new one lands.

Sketch (names illustrative):

```python
# The value refreshes centrally every 60s; sessions read the current value and
# rerun when a new one lands — no per-session timer, one shared computation.
@st.cache_data(refresh_every="60s")
def latest_metrics():
    return run_warehouse_query()

@st.fragment
def kpis():
    df = latest_metrics()          # returns the current cached value immediately
    st.metric("Orders", len(df))
    st.line_chart(df, x="ts", y="orders")

kpis()
```

- Split out from [#12980](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12980)

  off-thread cached computation; scheduled/recurring refresh is called out there
  as not-yet-built.

import pandas as pd

if st.button("Select the first row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [0], "columns": [], "cells": []}}
if st.button("Select no row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [], "columns": [], "cells": []}}

event = st.dataframe(
    df,
    key="data",
    on_select="rerun",
    selection_mode=["single-row"],
)

پاسخ پیشنهادی: آیا امکان دارد نمونه کد کامل برای آپلود فایل .ini به صورت تکی و همچنین آپلود پوشه حاوی فایل .ini را در مرورگر کروم ارائه دهید؟ این کمک می‌کند دلیل مشکل عدم بارگذاری فایل .ini هنگام آپلود پوشه بررسی شود.

شاهد مستند: متن رسمی؛ سازگاری نسخه باید بررسی شود.

بخش منبع:

```text
Where does st.file_uploader store uploaded files and when do they get deleted?
```

نسخهٔ منبع:

```text
695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd
```

متن شاهد:

```text
When you upload a file using [`st.file_uploader`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader), the data are copied to the Streamlit backend via the browser, and contained in a BytesIO buffer in Python memory (i.e. RAM, not disk). The data will persist in RAM until the Streamlit app re-runs from top-to-bottom, which is on each widget interaction. If you need to save the data that was uploaded between runs, then you can [cache](/develop/concepts/architecture/caching) it so that Streamlit persists it across re-runs.
```

نشانی منبع:

```text
https://github.com/streamlit/docs/blob/695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd/content/kb/FAQ/where-file-uploader-store-when-deleted.md
```

محدودیت: از گزارش مشخص است که آپلود فایل .ini به صورت تکی در کروم انجام می‌شود ولی هنگامی که به عنوان بخشی از پوشه است آپلود نمی‌شود. این رفتار پس از نسخه 1.60.0 استریم‌لیت رخ داده است. برای تحلیل دقیق‌تر و رد یا تأیید فرضیه مشکل در کد یا تنظیمات باید نمونه کد کامل بررسی شود.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: مشکل احتمالا مربوط به نحوه آپلود فایل های با پسوند .ini هنگام انتخاب پوشه در مرورگر کروم است و در نسخه‌های قبلی استریم‌لیت چنین مشکلی نبود.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

summary.problem:
*.ini files not uploaded when part of a folder with st.file_uploader, but upload fine as single file

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When uploading a folder containing a *.ini file using st.file_uploader the *.ini file is not uploaded.
Uploading the file when not part of a folder works
This is an issue with Chrome, but not an issue in firefox
It works in Streamlit version <=1.60.0

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
folder_path = st.file_uploader("**Upload files:**",accept_multiple_files = True, type=[".ini", ".txt"],)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Drag and drop a folder containing a *.ini file into a streamlit app (Streamlit v1.61.0 or later)running Chrome

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Expected Behavior

All the files in the folder should be uploaded

### Current Behavior

Only non *.ini files are uploaded

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version:3.13.1
- Operating System:Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome (Version 155.0.8059.27). Works with FireFox(157.0)


### Additional Information

_No response_

The data will persist in RAM until the Streamlit app re-runs from top-to-bottom, which is on each widget interaction. If you need to save the data that was uploaded between runs, then you can [cache](/develop/concepts/architecture/caching) it so that Streamlit persists it across re-runs.

متن شاهد:

```text
Based on the information given in this ticket, it looks like this is happening on an app running Streamlit 1.41.0. The [patch to fix the originally linked issue](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/9886) was shipped in Streamlit v1.45.0. Could you please update to the latest version of Streamlit (v1.45.1 as of writing), and see if that solves the issue for you? Thanks in advance!
```

نشانی منبع:

```text
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11500
```

محدودیت: اطلاعات موجود نشان می‌دهد که به‌روزرسانی به نسخه 1.45.1 در گذشته برخی خطاهای مشابه را رفع کرده است، ولی این خطا در نسخه 1.64.0 گزارش شده است. جهت تشخیص علت دقیق خطا و بررسی اینکه آیا مشکل مربوط به نسخه استریم‌لیت است یا مسائل دیگری، نیاز به نمونه کد واقعی دارید که خطا را بازتولید کند.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: خطای Cached ForwardMsg MISS ممکن است مرتبط با نسخه استریم‌لیت باشد ولی در نسخه 1.64.0 نیز رخ می‌دهد و بنابراین دلایل دیگری نیز ممکن است دخیل باشند.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.
